source_metadata.title: Efficacy and safety of empagliflozin for type 2 diabetes: a systematic review and meta-analysis

atoms.canonical_statement: The review aimed to assess the efficacy and safety of empagliflozin compared with placebo or other antidiabetic agents in adults with type 2 diabetes.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Aim: To assess the efficacy and safety of the novel sodium-glucose cotransporter 2 (SGLT2) inhibitor empagliflozin compared with placebo or other antidiabetic agents in patients with type 2 diabetes.

atoms.canonical_statement: The authors conducted a systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials and reported the review in accordance with PRISMA.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: We report our systematic review and meta-analysis in accordance with the recommendations set forth in the PRISMA statement.

atoms.canonical_statement: The literature search covered Medline, Embase, and the Cochrane Library from inception through 19 December 2013, conference abstracts/e-posters from 2009–2013, forward citation searching, the manufacturer website, and ClinicalTrials.gov through 17 March 2014.

Eligible studies were randomized controlled trials comparing empagliflozin with placebo or another antidiabetic medication in adults with type 2 diabetes, with intervention duration of at least 12 weeks; no language, year, or publication-status restriction was applied.

population.label: Adults with type 2 diabetes
inclusion_criteria: Empagliflozin compared with placebo or another antidiabetic medication

atoms.canonical_statement: Two reviewers independently screened records and full texts, with disagreements arbitrated by a third reviewer and resolved by consensus.
Two reviewers independently extracted study characteristics, participant characteristics, and efficacy/safety outcomes, with discrepancies resolved after consultation with a senior reviewer.
The primary efficacy outcome was absolute change in HbA1c from baseline.
Secondary efficacy outcomes were absolute changes in body weight, systolic blood pressure, diastolic blood pressure, and achievement of HbA1c <7%.

outcome.definition: Body weight, systolic/diastolic blood pressure, and HbA1c target attainment

atoms.canonical_statement: Safety outcomes included any hypoglycaemia, major hypoglycaemia requiring assistance, eGFR change, urinary and genital tract infections, volume-depletion adverse events, and all-cause mortality; cardiovascular outcomes were planned for extraction.

outcome.definition: Hypoglycaemia, major hypoglycaemia, eGFR, urinary/genital infections, volume depletion, mortality, and cardiovascular outcomes

atoms.canonical_statement: Meta-analyses were performed when at least three studies reported an outcome; analyses were separated by empagliflozin 10 mg vs 25 mg and by placebo vs active comparator, using inverse-variance random-effects WMDs for continuous outcomes and Mantel-Haenszel random-effects ORs for dichotomous outcomes.

Heterogeneity was assessed with Cochran Q and I², with I² >50% treated as high heterogeneity; a continuity correction of 0.5 was applied to trials with a zero event count in one arm, while trials with zero events in both arms were excluded from that analysis.
The review included 11 records describing 10 randomized studies with 6,203 participants.

atoms.canonical_statement: Seven included records were full-text publications and four were available only as abstracts and/or e-posters.

source_anchor.paragraph: Results of Search and Study Characteristics

atoms.canonical_statement: Included study duration ranged from 12 to 90 weeks; all trials included placebo comparison, while only three active-controlled comparisons involved metformin or sitagliptin.

source_anchor.paragraph: Results of Search and Study Characteristics

atoms.canonical_statement: Eight of the 10 included studies were rated at high risk of bias because last-observation-carried-forward was used to handle missing HbA1c data; the remaining two were rated at low risk of bias in the authors’ overall assessment.
All included randomized trials received industry funding.
The funnel plot was described as not asymmetric, and Egger testing did not detect small-study effects (p=0.56).
Empagliflozin 10 mg once daily reduced HbA1c versus placebo by WMD -0.62 percentage points (95% CI -0.68 to -0.57; I²=0%).

atoms.canonical_statement: Seven trials reported all-cause mortality: 5 deaths occurred among 2,874 participants in empagliflozin arms and 5 deaths among 1,704 participants in control arms.
None of the included trials reported cardiovascular outcome results.

In Supplementary Table S2, the review reports a placebo-corrected mean HbA1c change with empagliflozin 25 mg after 52 weeks of -0.66 percentage points (95% CI -0.88 to -0.44) for CKD stage 2 (eGFR 60-89 mL/min/1.73 m²).

population.label: Adults with type 2 diabetes and CKD stage 2 (eGFR 60-89 mL/min/1.73 m²)

atoms.canonical_statement: Only three active-controlled trials compared empagliflozin with metformin or sitagliptin, limiting comparative-efficacy conclusions.

atoms.canonical_statement: All included trials were short in duration and assessed surrogate endpoints, leaving long-term safety and hard clinical outcomes unresolved.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: All included trials were short in duration and assessed surrogate endpoints, leaving long-term safety and hard clinical outcomes unresolved.

atoms.canonical_statement: Use of LOCF for missing data in most included trials introduced bias, and the extent to which it influenced the pooled estimates was unknown.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Use of LOCF for missing data in most included trials introduced bias, and the extent to which it influenced the pooled estimates was unknown.

atoms.canonical_statement: Lack of participant-level data prevented assessment of effect modification in subgroups such as older adults or patients at high cardiovascular risk.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Lack of participant-level data prevented assessment of effect modification in subgroups such as older adults or patients at high cardiovascular risk.

atoms.canonical_statement: Direct trials comparing individual SGLT2 inhibitors were lacking.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Direct trials comparing individual SGLT2 inhibitors were lacking.

atoms.canonical_statement: The authors concluded that empagliflozin 10 mg and 25 mg similarly lower glucose and also reduce body weight and blood pressure; limited head-to-head data suggested glycaemic efficacy similar to metformin or sitagliptin without increased hypoglycaemia or urinary tract infection, while genital tract infections were increased and long-term cardiovascular safety remained unresolved.

A. Tsapas reported lecture fees from AstraZeneca and Boehringer Ingelheim and research support from Boehringer Ingelheim, Novartis, Novo Nordisk, and Sanofi; the remaining authors declared no competing interests.
